# Identity Read Reference

The `glassfrog me` command: the authenticated actor the token resolves to, with its organization and membership.

## Overview

`glassfrog me` is a top-level leaf command that calls the live GlassFrog API. It issues `GET /me`, decodes the response, and prints a reshaped identity projection to stdout. With `--include roles` it additionally requests the requester's roles in the same call (`?include=roles`).

The command makes exactly one request: no retry, no paging.

## Synopsis

```
glassfrog me [--include roles] [-o <format>] [--base-url URL]
```

- `-o, --output` and `--base-url` are persistent flags inherited from the root; they are accepted anywhere on the command path.
- Takes no positional arguments. An unexpected positional is a usage error.
- Output goes to stdout. Diagnostics and error messages go to stderr. The outcome class is also signalled by the exit code.

## Flags

| Flag | Scope | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--include` | Local to `me` | `roles` | Opt-in: embeds the requester's roles in the same read (maps to the API's `?include=roles`). Default absent → identity only. An unsupported target is rejected before any request is issued. |
| `--base-url` | Persistent, on the root | A URL | The GlassFrog API base URL — the highest-precedence rung of base-URL resolution (flag → `GLASSFROG_BASE_URL` → `.glassfrogrc base_url` → built-in default). Registered once on the root and inherited by every API command; `me` reads its value. |
| `-o`, `--output` | Persistent, on the root | `full` \| `compact` \| `json` \| `yaml` | Selects the output format for this invocation (default `full`). Inherited from the root and accepted anywhere on the command path. `full`/`compact` route the projection through the human templates; `json`/`yaml` emit the structured payload. See [Output Format Selection](output-format-selection.md). |

`--include` accepts a single supported target: `roles`. Any other value is rejected locally as a usage error naming the unsupported target, with no request issued.

## Output

On a `200` under the default `full` format, `me` prints a reshaped projection (not raw JSON). Each fact is on its own labelled line, in a stable order. The id values are always present. The token value never appears in the projection. Under `-o json` / `-o yaml` the same read is emitted as the structured payload instead (see [Output Format Selection](output-format-selection.md)).

Fields, in order:

| Field | Always present | Content |
|---|---|---|
| **actor** | Yes | Name, kind (`human` \| `agent`), and id (`per_…` for a human, `agt_…` for an agent). |
| **organization** | Yes | Name and id (`org_…`). |
| **access** | Yes | The membership access level: `admin` \| `normal`. |
| **roles** | Only with `--include roles`, when the response carries roles | One line per role: name and id (`role_…`). |

When `--include roles` is given but the actor fills no roles, the roles section is omitted entirely (no empty list is printed).

Illustrative shape (exact labels and glyphs are a build detail; the fields, their presence, and stable order are the contract):

```
actor:        Alice Smith (human) per_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
organization: Acme (org_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef)
access:       admin
```

With `--include roles` (roles present):

```
actor:        Claude (agent) agt_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
organization: Acme (org_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef)
access:       normal
roles:
  - Marketing Lead (role_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef)
  - Treasurer (role_00000000000000000000000000000001)
```

The roles embedded by `--include roles` carry the minimal shape (name and id). The comprehensive roles read is the `me roles` command (see My Roles reference); this embed is the API's convenience affordance, not a second roles command.

## Exit Codes

The exit code signals the outcome class. stdout carries the projection; `$?` carries the outcome; the two are orthogonal.

| Condition | Exit code | Category |
|---|---|---|
| Read succeeded, projection printed | `0` | Success |
| Unsupported `--include` target (no request issued) | `2` | Usage error |
| Unexpected positional argument | `2` | Usage error |
| No usable token (not authenticated) | `2` | Usage error |
| Bad base-URL configuration (flag / env / file) | `2` | Usage error |
| Malformed `.glassfrogrc` credential file | `1` | Internal error |
| 2xx body could not be decoded | `1` | Internal error |
| API answered non-2xx (any status, including `401` / `403` / `429`) | `3` | API error |
| API could not be reached (connection / DNS / TLS / timeout) | `6` | Network unavailable |

Any non-success outcome exits non-zero; an unmapped category falls through to `1`.

## Errors

Failure messages are written to stderr, are token-free, and each states the cause and a next step. The token value never appears in any message or in the projection.

| Condition | Exit code | stderr message (cause + next step) |
|---|---|---|
| No usable token | `2` | "not authenticated — run `glassfrog auth login` or set `GLASSFROG_TOKEN`" |
| Malformed credentials file | `1` | Names the file, then "fix or re-create it with `glassfrog auth login`" |
| Malformed base URL | `2` | Names the source, then "correct `--base-url` / `GLASSFROG_BASE_URL` / the `.glassfrogrc` `base_url`" |
| Transport failure | `6` | Names the cause, then "check connectivity — the API may be unreachable" |
| API answered non-2xx | `3` | Surfaces the HTTP status code (no tailored per-status next step) |

Every non-2xx response maps to `3` and surfaces the status code but not a tailored next step. Per-status meaning (e.g. `401` → re-authenticate, `429` → back off) is a later capability and is not part of this command's behavior.

## Notes

- Structured output is available: the persistent `-o, --output` flag selects `full` \| `compact` \| `json` \| `yaml`, so `me -o json` emits the structured payload. The reshaped projection above is the default (`full`) rendering. The flag is a cross-cutting root flag, not a `me`-local concern — see [Output Format Selection](output-format-selection.md). On failure under `json`/`yaml`, the cause-plus-next-step message still prints as text on stderr (structured failure rendering is not yet wired in).
- For the full resolution chain behind `--base-url` (env var, `.glassfrogrc`, default) and for token resolution (`GLASSFROG_TOKEN`, `.glassfrogrc token`), see the connection-configuration capability docs. This command introduces no env var or `.glassfrogrc` key of its own.
